_comment: THE SESSION TIMELINE STRIP — the one visual identity of this product.
This file is the ONLY place the class and mark ordinals live. scripts/gen_strip.py emits
them into Swift, TypeScript and Python. NOBODY HAND-TYPES THE INTEGERS.
Why that rule exists: during design, two independent proposals had classes 1 and 2 swapped
(1=agent,2=prompting vs 1=prompting,2=agent). A renderer fed the other spec's bytes paints
every agent run in the prompt colour — producing a plausible-looking strip showing a human
who typed for three hours straight. It does not crash, it does not look empty, and it
survives code review. With a Swift renderer AND a TypeScript renderer, that risk doubles.
spec/fixtures/*.json are decoded and asserted in BOTH languages for exactly this reason.
_byte_layout: bits 0-1 = class, bits 2-3 = density, bits 4-7 RESERVED and MUST be 0
_fill_rule: Column fill is PRIORITY-WEIGHTED ARGMAX OVER MILLISECONDS, not raw argmax and not majority.
MEASURED: a 71-minute session (the mean at tau=900) across 1024 columns is 4.2 s/column;
at a 400px render width it is 10.6 s/column. Essentially every column contains multiple
event types, so raw argmax erases prompting entirely — and prompting is only ~6% of events
(1,456 typed prompts vs 23,838 tool calls on the reference corpus).
_density_rule: events (tool_use + typed prompts) per second within the column, bucketed. This is the second channel that makes the bar read as a barcode rather than a solid block.
_resample_rule: 1024 -> W is ALWAYS nearest-neighbour on column centres. Never a box filter, never smoothing, in any renderer. A box filter averages ordinals, which is meaningless for a categorical channel.
_mark_rule: Marks carry absolute ms offsets and are stored SEPARATELY from columns so a 5-second prompt cannot be resampled away. They snap to the nearest output column centre and dedupe within markDedupeMinPx; a collapsed mark bumps that column's density by +1 so it can never vanish silently.
